newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Late Sri Lanka leader's daughter denies charges.
newsitem.headline: Late Sri Lanka leader's daughter denies charges.

text.p: The daughter of slain Sri Lankan president Ranasinghe Premadasa on Tuesday denied her father was involved in the 1988 assassination of President Chandrika Kumaratunga's husband, Vijaya.
"No amount of commission reports, insinuations or innuendos can ever tarnish...the good name and character of my father," Dulanjalee Jayakody said in a statement.

She was referring to last week's government announcement that a commission investigating the assassination of the popular actor-turned-politician, Vijaya Kumaratunga, had found the late president Premadasa was indirectly involved in the killing.
The Presidential Commission's report, issued on Friday, also said late Deputy Defence Minister Ranjan Wijeratne interfered with the police investigation into the case.
Vijaya Kumaratunga was gunned down by two motorcyclists on February 16, 1988. He had been expected to run in the 1989 presidential elections on a broad leftist ticket.
President Kumaratunga, who came to power in 1994, told a news conference on Friday: "(The commission had) definitely pointed their fingers at two individuals."

The commission report said: "The totality of the evidence ...establishes a prima facie case against President Ranasinghe Premadasa and Minister Ranjan Wijeratne, as to their indirect involvement in the assassination of Vijaya Kumaratunga."
Friday's report did not say what precise role Premadasa played in the killing, other than to say he was indirectly involved and that he had a clear motive.
"It was suggested that the motive for the assassination ... was that he became a formidable rival to Prime Minister Premadasa at the presidential stakes," the report said.
Premadasa was prime minister at the time of the assassination and won the presidential elections the next year.
Soon after the assassination, Premadasa's government blamed Vijaya's killing on left-wing JVP (People's Liberation Front) rebels who launched an abortive insurrection in the south of the country.
Jayakody, denying her father had any motive to have Vijaya Kumaratunga out of the way, said her father was nominated UNP presidential candidate eight months after the assassination.
Premadasa led the then-ruling United National Party (UNP), now the main opposition party, until he was killed by a suspected Tamil guerrilla in May 1993.
A UNP spokesman said the party would not comment on the report until party leaders had studied the 85-page document.
